messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Triggers → Memory
  - Triggers → Negative Appraisals
  - Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals → Triggers
  - Memory → Triggers

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Ricardo, a 70-year-old man with hands calloused from decades as a welder, carried a past that felt as immediate as the sparks flying from his torch. He had been a young man in his home country when the paramilitary forces swept through his village. He remembered the rough hands that seized him, the suffocating darkness of the makeshift prison, and the chilling certainty that he had no options, utterly trapped. The violence was relentless, punctuated by the terrifying crack of gunshots nearby, each sound a stark reminder of the fragile line between life and death. He vividly recalled the desperate pleas of others, and his own inability to intervene, a frozen terror that left him with a gnawing guilt. He was certain the event happened because of his perceived inaction, a deep-seated conviction that he should have done more to stop what happened, a self-blame that had festered for decades.

Now, years later and widowed, the world outside his welding shop in America held its own dangers. A sudden, sharp clang of metal, the backfire of a truck, or even the insistent ringing of a phone could plunge Ricardo back into that past. These auditory triggers, reminiscent of the gunshots he endured, immediately caused the memory to feel as if it were happening right now, the sounds echoing the very moment of his capture. When these triggers struck, the intense rage he felt during the torture would surge through him, an uncontrollable fury directed at his tormentors and, often, at himself. The memory’s visceral presence, coupled with this intense rage on recall, made him hypersensitive to anything that might bring it forward, effectively turning the memory itself into a potent trigger for further distress.

The constant threat of these re-experiencings shaped his daily life. When a trigger occurred, such as the loud, unexpected bang of a dropped pipe at work, Ricardo’s mind would instantly detach himself from the memories, a desperate attempt to create distance from the terrifying immediacy. He would also try hard not to think about the trauma at all, pushing any intrusive thoughts deep down. These maladaptive strategies, however, offered only temporary respite. His pervasive negative appraisal that you can never know who will harm you made him constantly vigilant, turning innocuous situations into potential threats. This heightened state of alert inadvertently increased the frequency of triggers; a casual glance from a stranger, or a sudden movement, could be misinterpreted, activating his underlying fear.

This deep-seated fear that you can never know who will harm you also dictated his interactions. He found himself becoming overly compliant when feeling even slightly threatened, whether by a demanding customer or a frustrated colleague. He would acquiesce to avoid any potential conflict, believing it was safer to appease than to assert himself. This fawning response, coupled with his ingrained inaction guilt, meant that any situation where he felt he had not adequately protected himself or others would compel him to suppress thoughts of the trauma, believing that dwelling on it only intensified his self-reproach.

Ricardo’s life had become a series of careful manoeuvres to avoid his triggers. He had grown increasingly isolated since his wife’s passing, finding solace only in the repetitive, solitary work of welding. Yet, even there, the sudden sparks and metallic noises could be overwhelming. When he tried to explain to his doctors or a sympathetic neighbour what had happened to him, he would lose the thread and simply couldn’t finish, the words getting stuck, the narrative too fragmented and painful to articulate coherently. This inability to clearly explain what happened only deepened his sense of isolation and reinforced his belief that no one could truly understand the horror he carried. He had finally sought help, exhausted by the relentless cycle of fear and rage, hoping to find a way to quiet the past that refused to stay there.

violation_explanations: The vignette does not explicitly state that triggers directly cause or reinforce Ricardo's negative appraisals or beliefs.
